subject: BYO KMS / audit log retention — product asks + triage
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BYO KMS / audit log retention — product asks + triage

Rachel,

Following up from yesterday's product sync — attaching the initial BYO/KMS feature brief and a CSV sketch of the log sampling we discussed. High level asks from Product and PMM: 

- Support a short-term retention carveout for BYO customers (30/90/365 windows) that maps to their KMS policies.
- Provide sampled audit exports (configurable sampling rate by tenant) to reduce export volume for large SaaS customers.
- Add a flag in the Admin Console to opt-in to higher-fidelity logging for audit windows during compliance reviews.

We need Security + Ops to triage feasibility, required telemetry changes, and a recommended default (product wants to ship a conservative default to avoid surprises). Specific questions for the triage: 

1) For retention windows tied to external KMS keys, how do we guarantee deletion semantics when KMS owner revokes access?
2) What minimal audit evidence can we produce for SOC2 attestation if we sample logs?
3) Estimated cost delta for ingest + storage at 10/50/100% sampling for a 1PB/yr workload (Ops estimate).

Can we set up a 30-minute triage this week? If you prefer, list the gaps and I'll take notes and follow up with the customer.

Attachments: redwood_byo_requirements_v1.pdf, log-sampling-proposal.csv

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr Product Manager — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYO KMS / audit log retention — product asks + triage

Marissa — thanks for the brief and the sample CSV. I skimmed the ask and pulled out a few clarifying points before we loop Security proper. Quick notes: 

- Retention tied to BYO KMS: we need to distinguish metadata retention from ciphertext retention. If a customer revokes KMS access, we can keep opaque ciphertext objects but cannot decrypt; are we comfortable representing that as "retained but inaccessible" in evidence? Ops has concerns about providing the appearance of deletion when secrets still exist encrypted — legal may want explicit deletion for some customers.

- Sampling and SOC2 evidence: sampling is OK for operational debugging, but compliance requests (e.g., a specific user action audit) usually require full fidelity for the requested window. We should define two evidence classes: "operational sample" (good for trends) and "compliance slice" (for forensic requests). How would we surface and request an on-demand full export?

- Cost delta ask: Ben, can you return rough T-shirt numbers (low/med/high) for the three sampling profiles in the CSV? Also include the ingestion impact for streamed realtime exports.

Let's do a 30-min triage today at 2:00pm PT. I'll invite Security if we hit unanswered legal/KMS semantics. Agenda: scope of evidence (sample vs compliance slice), deletion semantics for BYO keys, admin console controls and guardrails.

If Acme needs clarity before the triage, I'll include them in the calendar invite.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Compliance Programs (Interim)
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 13:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYO KMS / audit log retention — product asks + triage

Quick operational readout ahead of the 2pm triage: 

- Cost/ingest estimate (very rough): for a 1PB/yr customer ingest profile, sampling at 10% reduces export volume ~9x; storage savings are proportional but retention windows dominate cost beyond 90 days. T-shirt: 10% = low impact (~+10% infra ops), 50% = medium (+35%), 100% = high (+80%). I'll give a tighter number after I run the sampling sim tonight.

- Deletion semantics: currently we store encrypted audit blobs and separate metadata indices. If a customer revokes KMS keys, we automatically mark the blobs as inaccessible in the index and prevent logical access. Physical deletion (zeroing out encrypted blobs) requires an async background job and a retention policy change. For customers that require proof of physical deletion, we will need a new workflow with KMS escrow + deletion attestations. That's a product/security-ticket to scope.

- Operational guardrails: suggest default sampling rate = 10% for BYO, with a product prompt in the Admin Console that warns about compliance requests. Provide an "evidence request" button that triggers a temporary full-fidelity capture (rolling 7-day window) for a tenant; capture would spawn a short-term compute job and cost estimate.

I also attached a quick CSV with the sim plan (log-sampling-proposal.csv). See you at 2.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Acme Security <sec-ops@acme.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYO KMS / audit log retention — product asks + triage

Rachel/Ben/Marissa — thanks for the detail and for looping us in. A few clarifying items from our compliance team before the triage: 

1) For customers requiring legal deletion (not just inaccessible ciphertext), our contracts mandate a verifiable deletion certificate. Is Redwood able to support a deletion attestation signed by a KMS/HSM key controlled by the customer? If not, what are the timelines to design that?

2) Evidence request button: is the resulting "full-fidelity" capture scoped to specific tenants only, or will it capture cross-tenant traces? We need to understand blast radius and isolation.

3) For the sample vs compliance classification: in audits we typically ask for a complete stream of CRUD actions for the audit window. Would the 7-day temporary full capture hold raw events in plain text for the duration? If so, what controls exist around access and retention of that temporary store?

If possible, we'd appreciate a short pre-reads or a one-page summary on the deletion attestation and evidence workflow before the call so our counsel can triage with less back-and-forth.

Thanks — look forward to the triage.

—Priya S.
Priya Shah
Information Security Manager, Acme Corp
sec-ops@acme.com
